object_description: elongated three-story building with a walkable green roof
design_condition: The building is carefully embedded in the existing terrain and park, extending the green landscape onto its roof while preserving hedges and minimizing paved areas, though its proximity to the outdoor pool limits landscape continuity.

positive.statement: The roof landscape is a surprising and pleasing gesture that enlarges the outdoor space and strengthens the green oasis.
The architecture integrates independently into the park, with minimal paved areas benefiting the urban climate.
Separate routes for the public, athletes, and operations promise smooth operation.
The indoor pool clearly distinguishes dirty, wet, and clean areas.
The direct visual connection between the indoor and outdoor pools is very welcome.
Careful embedding into the existing terrain ensures an exceptionally small excavation volume.
The supporting concept is comprehensible and resource-saving in the intended construction method.
The insulated building shell ensures low winter heating requirements, while the green roof contributes to summer cooling.

negative.statement: The bicycle parking and right of way are too far from the main entrance.
The small distance from the outdoor pool weakens the landscape effect and spaciousness.
Better access to the park outside the bathing season would be desirable.
The permanent, low-maintenance design of the walkable green roof remains doubtful.
A substrate depth of only 20 centimetres may not ensure the required safety for roof use.
The facades lack functional summer heat protection.
The open ice rink is insufficiently shielded and would require additional noise protection.
The staging works, but its individual phases are sometimes too intertwined.
The address formation and impermeability along the street leave questions unanswered.
The green roof is a major cost driver and appears expensive to maintain.
